content: 1. Moynihan PJ and Kelly SA conducted a systematic review to evaluate the impact of restricting sugar intake on dental caries, providing evidence to inform WHO guidelines. 2. Griffin SO, Griffin PM, Swann JL, and Zlobin N studied the development of new coronal caries in older adults and discussed its implications for preventive strategies. 3. Broadbent JM, Thomson WM, and Poulton R investigated the progression of dental caries and tooth loss between the third and fourth decades of life through a birth cohort study. 4. Mejare I, Stenlund H, and Zelezny-Holmlund C conducted a 15-year prospective cohort study in Sweden to examine caries incidence and lesion progression from adolescence to young adulthood. 5. Fejerskov O explored the concepts of dental caries and their consequences for understanding the disease in a community dental and oral epidemiology context. 6. Thomson WM analyzed the experience of dental caries in older populations over time, drawing insights from large cohort studies. 7. Bernabe E and Sheiham A examined age, period, and cohort trends in caries of permanent teeth across four developed countries. 8. Bernabe E and Sheiham A also assessed the extent of differences in dental caries in permanent teeth between childhood and adulthood across 26 countries. 9. The first meeting of the Ad hoc Working Group on Science and Evidence for Ending Childhood Obesity, held in June 2014, addressed key issues related to childhood obesity. 10. Rugg-Gunn AJ, Hackett AF, Appleton DR, and Moynihan PJ analyzed the dietary intake of added and natural sugars among 405 English adolescents. 11. WHO published guidelines on sugar intake for adults and children, emphasizing the importance of reducing sugar consumption to improve health outcomes. 12. Rodrigues CS, Watt RG, and Sheiham A evaluated the effects of dietary guidelines on sugar intake and dental caries in 3-year-old children attending nurseries in Brazil. 13. Battellino LJ et al. conducted a longitudinal epidemiologic study to evaluate the oral health status of preschool children in Cordoba, Argentina, during 1993–1994. 14. Szanto S and Yudkin J investigated the effects of dietary sucrose on blood lipids, serum insulin, platelet adhesiveness, and body weight in human volunteers. 15. Reid M, Hammersley R, and Duffy M studied the effects of sucrose drinks on macronutrient intake, body weight, and mood state in overweight women over a 4-week period. 16. Takeuchi DDS conducted an epidemiological study on dental caries in Japanese children before, during, and after World War II. 17. Takeuchi M examined the relationship between dental caries incidence and sugar consumption in a study published in the Bulletin of Tokyo Dental College in 1960. 18. Takahashi K performed a statistical study on caries incidence in the first molar in relation to sugar consumption, published in the Japanese Journal of Oral Hygiene in 1959. 19. Takahashi K further analyzed caries incidence in the first molar and its association with sugar consumption in a study published in 1961. 20. Okuya Y conducted an epidemiological study on the relationship between caries incidence and sugar consumption in the second molar, published in the Journal of Dental Research in 1960. 21. Koike H studied caries incidence in the first molar in relation to sugar consumption among primary school children in Kyoto City, with findings published in the Bulletin of Tokyo Dental College in 1962. 22. Koike H also investigated the relationship between sugar consumption and caries incidence in primary school children in Kyoto City, with results published in the Journal of Okayama Medical Society in 1959. 23. The Global Status Report on Noncommunicable Diseases 2010 provided a comprehensive overview of the global burden of noncommunicable diseases and strategies for prevention and control.
